rounds.text: Waaree Technologies Ltd is showing a powerful operational turnaround that the market has not yet priced in, sitting at just 22% of its 52-week range [E4]. Trailing twelve-month sales have surged by 72% [E14], backed by a screen reason highlighting staggering sales growth of 115% year-over-year [E37]. Profitability is following suit with a 37% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E15], alongside net profit jumping 80% year-over-year [E39]. Operating margins have staged a remarkable recovery, expanding by 13 percentage points in the TTM period [E20] and leaping by 45 percentage points in the Sep 2026 quarter to reach positive territory at 2% [E21]. Results are scoring a maximum 100/100 for improving performance while sentiment and price remain overly cautious, presenting a classic mispricing where profit growth recently exceeded 1-year price growth by 64% [E33, E41]. Conceded: [E7, E11, E25, E27].

Waaree Technologies Ltd carries severe fundamental risks highlighted by a deeply negative book value of ₹ -6.14 yielding a price-to-book ratio of -30.94x [E1]. The company's profitability and capital returns are heavily distressed, evidenced by a terrible return on assets (ROA) of -27.57% [E7] and a negative ROCE of -32.2% [E11]. Long-term top-line stagnation further plagues the business, with compounded sales growth over a 3-year period collapsing by -38% [E13] alongside a meager 4% growth rate over a 10-year span [E12]. Financial strain is compounded by negative operational cash generation, with operating cash flow and free cash flow dropping to Rs -2.48 Cr and Rs -2.68 Cr respectively in March 2026 [E25, E26], while total borrowings rose to Rs 27.55 Cr by September 2026 [E27]. Furthermore, the company is officially flagged as having a low interest coverage ratio [E35], and promoter shareholding has slowly drifted downward by 1.89 percentage points down to 58.80% over recent years [E29]. Conceded: trailing twelve-month sales growth reached 72% [E14], profit growth hit 37% [E15], and quarterly operating margins showed a positive uptick in September 2026 [E21].

Conceded: negative book value and distressed return metrics [E1, E7, E11]. However, dismissing the business on these rearview-mirror metrics ignores a powerful, accelerating operational turnaround that renders stale sentiment obsolete [E41]. While the bear highlights long-term and 3-year historical sales struggles [E12, E13], it completely glosses over the massive inflection happening right now: trailing twelve-month sales growth has surged to 72% with profit growth at 37% [E14, E15], supported by screen signals noting sales spiking 115% YoY and net profit jumping 80% YoY [E37, E39]. Operating margins are actively staging a dramatic recovery, expanding by 13 percentage points in the TTM period and leaping by a remarkable 45 percentage points to 2% in the September 2026 quarter compared to the same period a year ago [E20, E21]. Conceded: cash flows were negative and borrowings ticked up [E25, E26, E27], but the company is starting to outperform expectations as profit growth outpaces 1-year price growth by 64% [E33]. The market is overly anchored to historical distress and is completely under-appreciating this explosive growth and margin inflection [E41].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month sales and profit growth show positive figures [E14, E15], along with a quarterly operating margin improvement to 2% in September 2026 [E21]. However, the bull's narrative of an explosive operational turnaround glosses over severe structural and balance-sheet decay that renders these short-term metrics deeply fragile. The company operates with a deeply negative book value of ₹ -6.14 leading to an extreme price-to-book ratio of -30.94x, alongside a catastrophic return on assets of -27.57% and a ROCE of -32.2% [E1, E7, E11]. Furthermore, despite the claimed margin inflection, operating cash flow and free cash flow remain strictly negative at ₹ -2.48 Cr and ₹ -2.68 Cr respectively as of March 2026, while borrowings have escalated to ₹ 27.55 Cr [E25, E26, E27]. This ongoing cash burn is compounded by explicit flags for a low interest coverage ratio and inconsistent yearly operating margins, proving that the underlying financial distress is far from resolved [E22, E35].
